content.title: About
content.content: Adobo is a traditional Filipino dish consisting of meat (usually chicken or pork) simmered in a sauce made from soy sauce, vinegar, garlic, onion and spices. The “Adobo with noodles” version adds boiled egg or wheat noodles to the classic sauce, making the meal heartier and convenient for quick service.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Adobo is considered the national dish of the Philippines and has many regional variations.
The word “adobo” comes from the Spanish “adobar” – “to marinate,” reflecting colonial influence.
The combination of vinegar and soy sauce allows the dish to be stored without refrigeration for a limited time.
Noodles are often cooked al dente before being mixed in, preserving texture during the final simmer.
Some versions incorporate coconut milk, giving the sauce a creamy note.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: The meat in adobo provides a high‑quality source of complete protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of vitamin B6
items.content: Vitamin B6 supports amino‑acid metabolism and nervous‑system function.

items.title: Probiotic‑like properties
items.content: The acidic environment created by soy sauce and vinegar can promote beneficial gut bacteria.

items.title: Energy‑providing carbs
items.content: Noodles add complex carbohydrates that deliver sustained energy and satiety.

items.title: Antioxidant compounds
items.content: Garlic and onion contain allicin and quercetin, which have antioxidant effects.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Soy sauce and the marinade can be very salty, which may be unsuitable for people with hypertension.

items.title: Soy allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to soy should avoid this dish.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Vinegar increases the dish’s acidity and may irritate the stomach of those with gastritis.

items.title: Fat content
items.content: Using pork can raise the amount of saturated fat.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve Adobo with noodles hot, garnished with fresh herbs such as cilantro or parsley. It can be eaten with a fork or chopsticks. Add a squeeze of lime or a dash of chili for extra brightness.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool the dish to room temperature, then store it in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Reheat on the stovetop or in a microwave, adding a splash of water to keep it moist.
